caption: Self-running, period 6: the dust on the obsidian powers the sticky piston beside it through the block; each push moves the redstone block off the dust and the stone into its cell, which points the dust at the TNT mid-push while the coral fan riding the slime pops and updates the TNT still at its source; the piston then loses power and pulls the frame back

One TNT per input pulse: the sticky piston pushes the slime frame north; the stone moving into the redstone block's cell points the dust at the TNT mid-push, and the coral fan riding the front slime pops when the slime behind it moves into its cell, priming the TNT while its moved copy lands; the release pulls the frame back

PRECISE: every primed TNT is at exactly the same point at fuse 1. The 12b duper with its stone swapped for a slime chain that carries a slime over the TNT cell during the push: every fresh TNT, whatever its random kick, is flung north at exactly vz = -1 with its z set exactly, stops against the wall (z exact, motion zeroed), drops into a 1-wide water channel flowing east that holds it against the east wall (x exact), resting on the floor (y exact)

Lever on/off: the 12b duper with an input beside its sticky piston: while the input is on, the piston is held extended and nothing dupes; switched off, it runs at 200 TNT/min again (first TNT 5 gt later)

SURVIVABLE: the precise duper judged with explosions ON (explode: on): every TNT explodes inside the water channel, where the water around the explosion (blast resistance 100) stops every ray before it reaches a block; 64 explosions in the judge run, the design intact and still duping in all 16 builds

LAUNCHED: the 12b duper with its stone swapped for a slime chain that carries a slime over the TNT cell during the push: every fresh TNT is flung north at exactly vz = -1.0 and vy = 0.1568 blocks/gt (only the cross axis keeps the random 0.02 kick); the judge measures the launch motion of every TNT

DROPPED straight down: the launching duper plus one stone as a north wall: every TNT is flung north, stops against the wall (its north-south position and motion exact) and falls straight down (horizontal motion under 0.01 blocks/gt at fuse 1), 72+ blocks by fuse 1
